title.narrative: Improving Family Health through access to safe water and sanitation

description.narrative: ACLO Potosi is a Jesuit NGO focusing on community development in rural areas in the Potosi department. Potosí is the poorest department of Bolivia with 88% of its rural population living in extreme poverty according to the government’s institute for statistics (INE). The communities of the Vitichi municipality, where this project will be implemented, are increasingly vulnerable to chronic water issues (shortage, salinity, contamination from mining), with 70% of families are suffering from water scarcity or limited access to potable water. This WASH project forms part of the Water and Gender Match Fund programme. The project aims to help the communities to set up drinking water and sanitation systems, improve their knowledge and practice of safe water consumption and hygiene and lobby for support from municipal governments in replicating the activities more widely. There will be a particular emphasis on working with women to empower them to play a key role in changing practice in the family and community domains to increase convenient availability of drinkable water and improve hygiene and sanitation.
